title: 1.25%: Japan's Rate Decision Lands Friday #Shorts
description:
Japan's interest rate is 1.25%. America's is 3.75–4%. That gap is why a decision in Tokyo can ripple across the world. On Friday 30 Oct the Bank of Japan makes its next call. Economists surveyed by CNBC expect a hold, with a hike seen in December or January. In August 2024, a rush to unwind this cheap-money 'carry trade' helped shake markets worldwide, and Japan's Nikkei fell more than 12% in a single day. What to watch: the yen (around 158 per dollar) and any hint about December.
Subscribe for the day's news explained in a minute.
Not financial advice. Hosts Arjun and Meera are AI. Made by AI. Made with hope.
Sources: CNBC (27 Oct 2026), FXStreet (28 Oct 2026), Japan Times and Bloomberg (28 Oct 2026), Yahoo Finance, Reuters/JPX (5 Aug 2024).
Footage: stock clips for illustration (Pixabay, NASA), not of the actual event.
#Shorts #WorldNews #NewsExplained #BankOfJapan #Yen

SCRIPT
ARJUN: "1.25 percent. That's Japan's interest rate, still far below America's. And this Friday, the Bank of Japan decides what's next."
MEERA: "Cheap money in Japan. Why would that matter to anyone else?"
ARJUN: "Because the US Fed's rate is 3.75 to 4 percent. That gap, roughly 2.5 to 2.75 points, lets investors borrow cheap yen and buy higher-yielding assets abroad. It's called the carry trade."
MEERA: "So what goes wrong?"
ARJUN: "When Japan's rates rise or the yen jumps, investors rush to repay and sell. On 5 August 2024, that unwind helped trigger a global sell-off. Japan's Nikkei fell more than 12 percent in one day, its worst day since 1987."
MEERA: "So what should we watch on Friday?"
ARJUN: "No decision yet. Economists surveyed by CNBC expect a hold, with a hike seen in December or January. Watch the yen, around 158 per dollar, and any hint about December."
MEERA: "The rate may not move Friday. The clue is what Japan signals next. Which will you watch: the rate or the yen? Comment below, and follow for daily news."

relevance.why: The story is still current. The BOJ meets 29–30 Oct and is widely expected to hold at 1.25%. The Fed held at 3.75–4% on 28 Oct, so the script's rate gap is correct. The risks are a global audience with little Japan interest, and the rule to hold the slot if the BOJ announces early.
